The affected elements: every element that has a relation or an inline reference (in the text or in a property marked `markdown`, SR-127) to the element, directly or through the chain (SR-024 AK1), each once at its shortest distance, breadth first, the element itself never. Distance 1: every element whose file holds a relation (any relation kind or relation-valued property) or an inline reference to it. From there onward along the derivation chain (meaning `derivation`, SR-013) and inline references that point at an affected element.

identifier.description: Its identifier (the value of its property with the meaning `identifier`, such as SR-036, #305), for display next to `shortId`; left out when it has none.

distance.description: Steps from the element: 1 when this element's file points at it directly.

path.description: The way: the element asked for first, this element last, each element in between that points at the one before it; each named by UUID and repository (D-058).

via.description: How this element points at the one before it on the path: a relation stored under `key` (a relation kind or a relation-valued property), or an inline reference in its text or in a property marked `markdown`.

total.description: The number of all affected elements; `affected` holds the page of `limit` from `offset`.

records.description: The evidence records of an older version of the element (SR-024 AK4): its records in the evidence folders (SR-028, SR-093) whose `version` is not its current one, newest first. Empty when its current version cannot be computed (its file no longer holds it, an embedded image cannot be read).

incomplete.description: True while a repository of the workspace file is not on this machine: elements there may point at the element (SR-006 AK2).

commands.name: trace.neighbourhood
commands.title: Show neighbourhood
commands.summary: The surroundings of one element over every relation kind and inline reference, up and down to a depth; each edge says whether it repeats an element and whether it is outdated. One page of nodes at a time.

repository.description: The workspace name of the repository of the element ref names, as in element.get (#255).

direction.description: `up`: along the links the element's file stores (its parents, the targets of its other relations and relation properties, its inline references). `down`: along the links that point at it (its children and every element whose file has a relation or an inline reference to it). The source of a link is placed below its target (ADR-0004).

maxDepth.description: The deepest depth in each direction; 0: the root only. Omitted: 1 (the direct neighbours), unless `allLevels` is true.

allLevels.description: Walk as far as the links go (the whole chain); not together with `maxDepth`. For the chain alone ask with `meanings: ["derivation"]`.

kinds.description: Keys of relation kinds or of properties of kind `relation` (such as `packages`) to follow. An unknown key is `input.invalid`. See `meanings` for the filter rule.

meanings.description: Relation kinds with these meanings are followed; `reference` stands for inline references. Without `kinds` and `meanings` every relation and reference is followed. Otherwise a link is followed when its key is in `kinds` or its meaning is in `meanings`; an empty list follows nothing.

limit.description: Nodes of the page; total counts all.

offset.description: Nodes skipped before the page, in the order of `nodes` (the root, the up walk level by level, the down walk level by level).

nodes.description: Every element reached once per walk, at its shortest depth: the root, then the up walk, then the down walk, each level by level. In a view only the elements that apply in it (SR-040); the root always. Only the page of `limit` nodes from `offset` is listed; `total` counts all.

identifier.description: Its identifier (the value of its property with the meaning `identifier`, such as SR-036, #305), for display next to `shortId`; left out when it has none.

depth.description: Steps from the root in its walk: 0 for the root.

direction.description: `up` for an element reached along the links its file stores, `down` for one reached along the links that point at it; left out for the root.

expanded.description: Its links were looked at; false only at `maxDepth`, where the walk was cut.

total.description: The number of all nodes; `nodes` holds the page.

edges.description: Every link the walks followed, up edges first, then down edges, in walk order; an edge is on the page of the node it leads to in its walk. A hub (a package with many members) can put many edges on one page: leave out `packages` with `kinds` or `meanings`. Not listed: unresolved links (`element.get` and `workspace.check` report them).

source.description: The element whose file stores the link.

sourceRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `source`.

target.description: The element the link points at (ADR-0004), whatever the walk direction.

targetRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `target`.

link.description: A relation in the frontmatter or an inline reference in the text or in a property marked `markdown`.

kind.description: The frontmatter key, only for `link: relation`.

property.description: The key is a property of kind `relation` (such as `packages`), not a relation kind.

meaning.description: The meaning of the relation kind, `reference` for an inline reference; left out for a kind without a meaning and for a property.

cyclic.description: Both ends lie in one cycle of the walk.

repeated.description: The edge leads, in its walk, to an element that this walk first reached through another edge, or to the root: a repetition (SR-107 AK3). It holds within one call (asking again from a child loses it; to open a tree level by level ask from the same root with a larger `maxDepth`) and within the followed kinds (the tree of derivations comes from `meanings: ["derivation"]`). First means first reached breadth first (spec question #421).

outdated.description: The link stores a version of normal form 1, its target is available and has a current version, and the two differ (SR-025).

commands.name: trace.matrix
commands.title: Show traceability matrix
commands.summary: Traceability matrix of a selection: one row per element in list order, one column per relation kind and direction that occurs, each cell the elements at the other end with outdated and missing marks; per column how many rows have a link. One page of rows at a time. With evidence locations also each requirement's test cases and verification status, and the degree.

selection.description: The rows: every element the selection selects, as `element.list` selects them (every part given must hold, SR-101 AK2). In a variant view (`selection.view`, or the view of the saved filter) a link whose other end does not apply in the view is left out of the cells and the counts (SR-040), as `trace.neighbourhood` leaves it out of its walk.

sort.description: As in `element.list`: the rows are in the order `element.list` gives for the same `selection` and `sort` (SR-125 AK1). Without `sort`, the sort of the saved filter in `selection.filter`. `hierarchy` first makes the rows the derivation tree and gives each row its `depth`.

kinds.description: Keys of the relation kinds or of properties of kind `relation` (such as `packages`) to make columns of. An unknown key is `input.invalid`. Without `kinds`, the columns are the relation kinds of the metamodel (Beziehungsarten, D-043, D-037): relation properties such as the package and the validity are their own built-in meanings (D-012) and form a column only when named here; inline references are no relation kind and never form a column.

limit.description: Rows of the page; `total` counts all.

offset.description: Rows skipped before the page, in the order of the list.

columns.description: One column per relation kind and direction that occurs in the whole selection (SR-125 AK2), not only on the page: a kind or direction no row has makes no column. Order: relation kinds in the order of the metamodel, then properties of kind `relation` in property order; per key `out` before `in`. `type` says what a column holds and so the shape of its cells; every column is `relation`. The evidence columns (SR-126) are no column type: their header is `evidence` and their cells are `rows[].testCases` and `rows[].verification`, so a reader of `columns` and `cells` needs no other shape.

type.description: The column holds relations: its cell in each row is an array of relations (`data-export#/$defs/relation`) of `kind` and `direction`. The evidence columns of SR-126 are `evidence`, `rows[].testCases` and `rows[].verification`, not a column type.

kind.description: Key of the relation kind, or of the property of kind `relation`.

property.description: `kind` is the key of a property of kind `relation`, not of a relation kind.

meaning.description: The meaning of the relation kind; left out for a kind without a meaning and for a property.

direction.description: `out`: the relations the row element's file stores. `in`: the relations of other elements that point at it.

name.description: For `out`, the `name` of the kind (e.g. Derives from); for `in`, its `inverse-name` (e.g. Derived by), the `name` when it has none. A name can be the same for both directions (Distinct from): `direction` tells them apart.

count.description: How many rows of the whole selection have at least one relation in this column (SR-125 AK3), whatever state its other end is in; a relation to a missing target counts. With a view, the relations the cells show.

share.description: `count` divided by `total`: the share of the rows of the whole selection.

rows.description: The page: one row per element of the list, in its order (SR-125 AK1).

repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the element.

identifier.description: Its identifier (the value of its property with the meaning `identifier`, such as SR-036), for display next to `shortId`; left out when it has none.

depth.description: Only when `sort` starts with `hierarchy`: the depth of the element in the derivation tree, as `element.list` gives it in `tree`.

testCases.description: SR-126 AK1, AK2: only with `evidence`, on a row whose type has the meaning `requirement` and that applies in its view. The test cases that name the requirement, with their verification executions that hold in the view of `evidence` (`trace.chain` shows the same test cases in the same view), by class name then name; an empty array when it has none: a gap (AK2). Records without a test case (inspection, analysis, a manual record without `test-case`) are not here; they count for `verification` only (spec question #528 Q3). The chain and `evidence.list` give every execution.

name.description: The JUnit `name`, or the `test-case` of the Markdown records.

className.description: The JUnit `classname`; left out for a test case of Markdown records.

executed.description: The test case has at least one execution of this requirement in the view (SR-033 AK3).

last.description: The last execution (letzte Durchführung): the newest execution of this requirement in the view, of any version, with result, date, item and version; its record file (`repository`, `file`, `line`) is the Beleg of a JUnit execution. Left out when `executed` is false.

mark.description: How the cell is marked (AK2; spec questions #528 Q1, Q2 and #593 Q2), the first that holds: `not-executed` when `executed` is false; `outdated` when `last` is of another version than the requirement's current one, or its current version is not known; `failed` when `last` failed. Left out when the last execution passed for the current version.

verification.description: SR-126 AK1, AK3: only with `evidence`, on a row whose type has the meaning `requirement` and that applies in its view. Its verification status in the view of `evidence`, one entry, the same as `element.get` and `evidence.status` give for that view: `indirect` when it is verified through its children (AK3).

cells.description: One cell per entry of `columns`, in the same order; a cell takes its shape from the type of its column. For `relation`, an array of the relations of the row element in the column's `kind` and `direction`, each with `shortId` and `title` of the other end when it is available (SR-125 AK2), and an empty array when it has none: a gap (AK3). Outgoing relations come in the order of the file, incoming ones in the order of the incoming index (store order). A relation to an older version of its target is `outdated`, one to a target that is not there has `targetState: "missing"` (SR-125 AK4); for an incoming relation, `outdated` means its source stores an older version of the row element and `currentVersion` is the row element's.

total.description: The number of rows of the whole selection.

incomplete.description: The selection is incomplete (SR-006 AK2), or the workspace file lists a repository that is not on this machine: relations of elements there that point at a row cannot be seen, and its elements may belong to the selection. With `evidence`, also when an evidence location lies in such a repository: its records are not seen (SR-006 AK2).

evidence.description: The header of the evidence columns (SR-126): given when the workspace file names an evidence location, the metamodel is valid and the selection holds an element whose type has the meaning `requirement` (spec question #593 Q1); then every requirement row of the page that applies in `view` has `testCases` and `verification`. Other rows have neither (a requirement valid only in variants, without a view): not applicable, no gap. Left out otherwise, and the output is the one of SR-125.

view.description: The one view of the test cases, the status and the degree: the selection's view, else its saved filter's, else the core (as `evidence.degree`; spec questions #593, #592 Q1). `element.get` and `evidence.status` give every view.

degree.description: SR-126 AK4: the verification degree of the whole selection in `view`, with the count per status, not of the page only; the same as `evidence.degree` gives for the same selection (SR-037).

names.description: The elements that `evidence` and the rows' `verification` name by UUID only, each once in the order first named: the variant of the view and the missing children (`missingChildren`), so a reader names them by short ID, identifier and title (#588). Left out when they name none.

commands.name: trace.graph
commands.title: Show graph
commands.summary: The graph of one element: what its links lead to above it and what links to it below, to a depth, over the chosen kinds. Each element is one node with its level and marks, and each link between two nodes is one edge. At most `limit` nodes, nearest levels first.

repository.description: The workspace name of the repository of the element ref names, as in element.get (#255).

maxDepth.description: The deepest level in each direction; 0: the element only. Omitted: 1 (the direct neighbours), unless `allLevels` is true.

allLevels.description: Go as far as the links go (the whole chain), within `limit`; not together with `maxDepth`. For the chain alone ask with `meanings: ["derivation"]`.

kinds.description: Keys of relation kinds or of properties of kind `relation` (such as `packages`) to follow. An unknown key is `input.invalid`. See `meanings` for the filter rule.

meanings.description: Relation kinds with these meanings are followed; `reference` stands for inline references. Without `kinds` and `meanings` every relation and reference is followed. Otherwise a link is followed when its key is in `kinds` or its meaning is in `meanings`; an empty list follows nothing.

limit.description: The most nodes, the element included; the nearest levels first (`truncated` says when more exist).

nodes.description: Every element of the graph once: the element first, then level by level from the nearest (for each distance the elements above, then those below, each in the order the links were followed). An element reached both ways is one node at its smaller distance, above on a tie. In a view only the elements that apply in it (SR-040); the element always. At most `limit` nodes.

identifier.description: Its identifier (the value of its property with the meaning `identifier`, such as SR-036, #305), for display next to `shortId`; left out when it has none.

expanded.description: Its links in the direction of its level (both for the element) were looked at and every element they lead to is a node. False at `maxDepth`, where `limit` stopped the walk, and when `limit` left out an element they lead to.

level.description: 0 for the element; -d for an element reached d steps up along the links the files store (its parents, the targets of its other relations and relation properties, its inline references), +d for one reached d steps down along links that point at it. The source of a link is placed below its target (ADR-0004).

marks.description: In this order, only those that hold (SR-111 AK4): `outdated`, the element stores an outdated relation, relation property or inline reference (SR-025, the `relation.outdated` hints of element.get), whatever kinds are followed; `superseded`, its status is one the metamodel marks invalid (D-044); `no-evidence`, the gap rule of trace.chain (SR-022 AK3): a requirement without a derivation child that applies in the view and without evidence, whatever depth is shown. Evidence records come in stage 4: until then every requirement without a child is `no-evidence`. Empty when none holds.

edges.description: Every followed link from one node to another, also one the walks did not take (a link between two parents, or from a child to a parent): by source in the order of `nodes`, then in the order its file stores them (relations and relation properties in frontmatter order, then inline references). A link from an element to itself is no edge. Not listed: unresolved links (`element.get` and `workspace.check` report them).

source.description: The element whose file stores the link.

sourceRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `source`.

target.description: The element the link points at (ADR-0004).

targetRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `target`.

link.description: A relation in the frontmatter or an inline reference in the text or in a property marked `markdown`.

kind.description: The frontmatter key, only for `link: relation`.

property.description: The key is a property of kind `relation` (such as `packages`), not a relation kind.

meaning.description: The meaning of the relation kind, `reference` for an inline reference; left out for a kind without a meaning and for a property.

outdated.description: The link stores a version of normal form 1, its target has a current version, and the two differ (SR-025).

truncated.description: More elements are reachable than shown: `limit` stopped a walk or left out a node. The nodes kept are the nearest ones.

problems.description: Hints: `metamodel.meaning-unassigned` when no relation kind has the meaning `derivation` or no type the meaning `requirement`, so `no-evidence` cannot be found (SR-013 AK3).

commands.name: hint.list
commands.title: List hints
commands.summary: Open hints of the workspace, filterable by kind, type, package or variant.

kind.description: Only hints with one of these codes.

type.description: Only hints about elements of one of these types, or of a type that extends one of them (SR-012).

package.description: Only hints about elements whose property with the meaning packages lists this package.

variant.description: Only hints about elements that apply in this variant by their validity: those without a validity and those whose validity lists it (SR-040).

ref.description: Only the hints about this element.

hints.description: The open hints: findings of severity warning about one element (glossary "Hinweis": the element should be checked; it blocks nothing and changes no status), from the same whole-workspace findings as workspace.check; errors, info and warnings about no element are not hints. Filters combine with AND. Each hint with its kind (code), the element it is about (elementId, repository, file, line), its target where it has one (targetId) and its reason (message; for an outdated relation with both versions and their dates, D-013). In the order of workspace.check.

incomplete.description: True while a repository of the workspace file is not on this machine: the hints of its elements are not listed (SR-006 AK2).

commands.name: hint.confirm
commands.title: Confirm hints
commands.summary: Confirm hints, by ID (hintIds) or all of one element (ref, target): writes the current target version into the relation or inline reference (in the text or in a property marked `markdown`, SR-127), and nothing else but the current titles of the file's same-repository targets (D-042); an ID no open hint has gives a warning, for example one confirmed already.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Writes the current version of the target, which depends on the metamodel (which properties count).

input.description: Give `hintIds`, `ref`, `target` or several of them; none is `input.invalid`. `ref` and `target` select the open confirmable hints (those with a `hintId`, as hint.list gives them) about `ref` and pointing at `target`, both when both are given; `kind` narrows only that selection and needs `ref` or `target`. The selected hints and `hintIds` are confirmed together, as one set (SR-027 AK2): each once, `confirmed` names `hintIds` first, then the selected IDs. A selection without an open confirmable hint is a `hint.not-found` warning.

hintIds.description: IDs of hints to confirm (`hintId` of hint.list).

ref.description: Confirm the open confirmable hints about this element: the outdated relations and inline references (in the text and in properties marked `markdown`) its file stores.

target.description: Confirm the open confirmable hints on relations and inline references that point at this element, for example after it changed.

kind.description: Only selected hints with one of these codes (with `ref` or `target`).

commands.name: element.search
commands.title: Search elements
commands.summary: Full-text search over title, text, properties and IDs of the elements of a selection, typo tolerant, in any case, the best first.

query.description: Words split at spaces; every word must match (in the title, the text, a property value, the type or status name, or an ID). A word matches words it begins (from 2 letters) and with a typo (1 edit from 4 letters, 2 from 8; none for a query word with a digit), in any case. A short ID, an identifier or at least 6 hex digits of a UUID match that element exactly; ID matches come first. A query without a word finds nothing.

selection.description: Search only within it (SR-068 AK3): a view, a filter, a package or IDs.

fields.description: Search only these: `title`, `text` (the Markdown text), `properties` (every other value, type and status names; not relations), `id` (UUID, short ID, identifier). Default all.

output.description: One page of the hits, the best first: ID matches, then relevance, then workspace order. Waits for the search index while it is built.

repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the element.

identifier.description: The value of the property with the meaning identifier, when the element has one.

status.description: The status key as written in the file.

score.description: Relevance of the matched words, rounded to 6 significant digits; 0 for an ID match only.

fields.description: What a word of the query was found in.

terms.description: The words of the element that matched, in lower case, for highlighting; none for an ID.

commands.name: filter.list
commands.title: List saved filters
commands.summary: Saved filters of the workspace, with their definitions.

file.description: The filter file, relative to the workspace root.

filters.description: In the order of their files. A faulty file is not listed; it is one of `problems`.

problems.description: Filter files that cannot be read, do not match filter.schema.json, or repeat the name of an earlier file.

commands.name: filter.save
commands.title: Save filter
commands.summary: Save a named filter as YAML in the repository; an existing name replaces that filter.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Checks the sort of the filter against the metamodel, which is missing or faulty.

where.description: Checked as in a selection; element references are written as UUIDs.

sort.description: Order of element.list with this filter when its input gives no sort.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

commands.name: evidence.list
commands.title: List evidence
commands.summary: Evidence records of an element with version, item, date, result, evidence location and baselines that contain the version.

view.description: `core`: only the records without a variant; a variant: only the records for that variant (SR-047 AK1, AK2); absent: every record of the element.

records.description: The evidence records of the element (SR-028, SR-093), newest first, each with its version, item, date, result and evidence (SR-032 AK1) and the baselines that contain its version (`baselines`, SR-032 AK2; empty when none does).

testCases.description: The test cases that name the element (SR-033), by class name, then name, each with the element's own records only, newest first, and every kind of record as in `records`; with `view` only the executions that hold in it, and a test case all of whose executions hold in another view is left out (a test case that was only skipped stays, `executed` false).

problems.description: Findings in the baseline files (`baseline.invalid`, `file.invalid-yaml`, ...): a baseline file that cannot be read names no baseline in `baselines`.

incomplete.description: True when an evidence location or the baselines folder lies in a repository that is not on this machine: records or baselines there are not seen (SR-006 AK2).

commands.name: evidence.record
commands.title: Record evidence
commands.summary: Write a manual verification or validation record (Markdown, evidence-record.schema.json) into an evidence folder of the workspace; the element's UUID and current version are filled in. A verification names a requirement, a validation a need or a requirement (D-012). Never replaces a file: a name that is taken gets -2, -3, ...
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Fills in the current version of the element, which depends on the metamodel (which properties count).

ref.description: The element the record is about. Its UUID and current version are written into the record; neither is an input (D-026).

kind.description: Verification (Nachweis) of a requirement, or validation of a need or a requirement (D-007, D-012). A validation record counts for the validation status only (SR-030 AK3).

item.description: The item under test (Prüfling), for example the build or sample. Required for verification. No white space at either end and no control characters other than tab, line feed and carriage return.

variant.description: A variant the element applies in (an element whose type has the meaning variant); the record holds for it. Absent: the core.

date.description: When the check was done. Default: the time of the call, UTC, whole seconds. Its first ten characters (the day in its own offset) start the file name.

evidence.description: Where the Beleg is: a path relative to the record file, a file URL or any URI. Written as given; ReqSeq never opens it (D-007).

testCase.description: Optional test case name or ID (`test-case` in the file, SR-033).

folder.description: The folder to write into: an evidence location of the workspace file or a folder below one, relative to the workspace root (the folder of the main repository) with `/`, for example `evidence/manual` or `../tests/evidence`. Missing folders below the location are created. Default: the first evidence location whose repository is on this machine.

items.description: The written record file, relative to the workspace root as `workspacePath` gives it (with `/`).

record.description: The record as the Markdown reader reads it back from the written file (`source: markdown`, its repository and file, line 1), with the UUID and current version of the element.

commands.name: evidence.enrichJunit
commands.title: Enrich JUnit file
commands.summary: Add UUID, version, item and date to every test case of a JUnit XML file that names an element by short ID, UUID or identifier. Test cases with an unknown reference stay unchanged and are listed; the CLI exits 1.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Writes the current versions of the elements, which depend on the metamodel (which properties count).

file.description: The JUnit XML file to enrich. It is rewritten in place unless `output` is given. A test case that already has a `reqseq:version` is never changed (D-026).

item.description: The item under test (Prüfling), for example the build. No white space at either end and no control characters other than tab, line feed and carriage return.

date.description: The date of the test run. Default: an existing `reqseq:date` of the test case, else the `timestamp` of its test suite when that has a time zone, else the time of the call.

output.description: Default: overwrite the input file. An existing file is replaced only when it is a JUnit XML file the scanner accepts; its folder must exist.

testCases.description: The test cases that name at least one element and are enriched: by this call, or already before.

unknown.description: Each reference that names no element or more than one, with its test case; that test case stays unchanged.

line.description: The line of the `<testcase>` in the file as read.

files.description: The written file, relative to the workspace root (the folder of the main repository) with `/` when it lies below it or in another repository of the workspace, else its absolute path. None when nothing is written: nothing to change in place, or `output` holds these bytes already; a given `output` is otherwise written even when nothing changes.

commands.name: evidence.status
commands.title: Show evidence status
commands.summary: Verification status of a selection per view, from the evidence records (SR-031) and, without own record, from the children with the children that are missing (SR-034); validation status from the validation records (SR-038).

elements.description: One page of the selection in workspace order, each element as element.list gives it, with `verification` for every element whose type has the meaning `requirement`: its verification status (SR-031, ADR-0012 "Status rules") in the core and in each variant it applies in (SR-040, SR-047), and for a requirement without own verification record in a view its indirect verification from its children (`indirect`) or the children that are missing (`missingChildren`, SR-034); an element marked emergent (SR-035) is never `indirect`; and `validation`, the validation status (SR-038, `$defs/element` `validation`: every need, any other element with a validation record). Derived from the evidence records; it is not the element's `status` and never changes it (D-030). While the metamodel is not valid the records are not compared: every requirement is `open`, every need `open`, and no other element has `validation`.

total.description: Every element of the selection, not only the page.

incomplete.description: A repository of the workspace is not available here (SR-006 AK2): its elements, and the records of its evidence locations, are missing.

names.description: The elements that `verification` names by UUID only, each once in the order first named: the variants of its views and the missing children (`missingChildren`), so a reader names them by short ID, identifier and title (#588). Left out when it names none.

commands.name: evidence.coverage
commands.title: Show evidence coverage
commands.summary: Coverage of a selection per level: how many have children, how many have evidence; with the element lists.

selection.description: The elements to cover, as `element.list` takes them; every part given must hold (SR-101 AK2). Its view (else the view of its saved filter) narrows the children to those that apply in it, as the chain does; evidence records count for that view, else for the core, as the filter condition `verification` does.

levels.description: One level per element type of the selection with the meaning `need` or `requirement` (a subtype is its own level), in metamodel order (spec question #527). Elements whose status the metamodel marks invalid are not counted (SR-036 AK4, D-044); other types have no level.

total.description: The counted elements of the type.

withChildren.description: How many have a derivation child that counts: one whose status is not marked invalid and, with a view, that applies in it; in any repository.

withEvidence.description: Only for a type with the meaning `requirement`: how many have at least one verification record in the view (the core without one), of any version and result (`hasVerificationRecord`, spec question #527).

elements.description: The UUIDs behind every number, in selection order (SR-036 AK2): pass them as `selection.ids` to `element.list`. `withEvidence` and `withoutEvidence` only where the level has `withEvidence`.

names.description: Every element of `levels[].elements`, each once in selection order, so a reader names them by short ID, identifier and title (#588). Left out when no level lists an element.

commands.name: evidence.degree
commands.title: Show verification degree
commands.summary: Verification degree of a selection in one view: the share of the requirements verified or indirect, and the count per verification status (SR-037).

selection.description: The requirements to count, as element.list takes them. Its view (else its saved filter's, else the core) is the view of the status.

view.description: core, or the variant of the selection's view (else of its saved filter's).

names.description: The variant of `view` (#588), so a reader names it by short ID and title. Left out in the core.

commands.name: evidence.withoutPassedTest
commands.title: List requirements without passed/no test
commands.summary: Every requirement without a passed test execution in one view (SR-120): no verification record with method test and result passed, of any version, holds there (spec question #532). Each with its verification status.

view.description: Default: the core. A variant: only records for it count, and only requirements that apply in it (SR-047).

elements.description: One page, by type, then identifier, else short ID: every requirement (type with the meaning `requirement`, status not marked invalid, applies in the view) without a verification record with method `test` and result `passed` that holds in the view, of any version and also when a later run failed (spec question #532). Each as evidence.status gives it, with `verification` and `validation`.

total.description: Every listed requirement, not only the page.

view.description: core, or the variant of the view.

incomplete.description: A repository of the workspace, or of an evidence location, is not on this machine: its requirements, or a passed test there, are not seen (SR-006 AK2).

names.description: The elements that `verification` names by UUID only, each once in the order first named: the variant of the view and the missing children (`missingChildren`), so a reader names them by short ID, identifier and title (#588). Left out when it names none.

commands.name: data.export
commands.title: Export data
commands.summary: Data of the current state as JSON for external evaluation, or, from the command line and the API, as JSON Lines with one element per line: every element unless a selection is given, so an evaluation selects by filter, package, baseline or variant instead of exporting everything; no paging. With `data store` the only commands so far that take `selection.baseline`: the elements the baseline lists, as they are now. `data store` writes a whole state to a file.

commands.name: data.store
commands.title: Store data
commands.summary: Write the data of the current state (as data export gives it) as JSON Lines, one element per line, to `<commit>.jsonl` in a folder; `-dirty` with uncommitted ReqSeq files, replaces the file of the same commit; an old `<commit>.json` stays as it is. Many such files load as one table, grouped by `commit` and `dirty`. One folder per selection: the name is the same for every selection. Takes `selection.baseline` as `data export` does.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Stores the data of the current state with the versions of its elements, which depend on the metamodel (which properties count).

folder.description: Folder for the file; created when missing inside a repository of the workspace (also an ignored one), must exist outside.

items.description: Written file: relative to the workspace root when it lies in a repository of the workspace, else absolute.

commands.name: variant.diff
commands.title: Show variant difference
commands.summary: What a variant adds, replaces and excludes compared to the core.

commands.name: variant.exclude
commands.title: Exclude requirements from variant
commands.summary: Exclude core requirements for a variant; written into the variant file only.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Writes a variant file, and no change can be checked against a missing or faulty metamodel.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

commands.name: baseline.create
commands.title: Create baseline
commands.summary: Write a baseline file for a selection (SR-050, ADR-0018): name, date, the HEAD commit of every repository involved, ID and version of every element. Refused while files of the selection are not committed. Never commits, never replaces a baseline.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Stores the current versions of the selection, which depend on the metamodel (which properties count).

selection.description: Stored in the file: a saved filter as its where and view, package and view with their title. Not baseline.

output.description: Errors: baseline.exists when a baseline has the name, ignoring case and Unicode normal form (details.file, details.repository: its file; nothing written, SR-050 AK6); a taken file name gets -2, -3, …; baseline.uncommitted-changes (details.elements[] {id, repository, file}, details.files[] {repository, file}; SR-050 AK2); git.unavailable when a repository involved is not under Git or has no commit (details.repository; AK7); file.faulty when a selected element has no version (details.elements[]); input.invalid for selection.baseline. The baseline is never replaced afterwards.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root, / as separator.

file.description: The file, relative to the workspace root, / as separator.

repository.description: The repository that holds the file; `repository` in the file is relative to it.

elements.description: Number of elements in the file.

incomplete.description: A repository is not here, so the view may miss a replacement or exclusion stored there (SR-006); the file is written all the same, with a warning.

commands.name: baseline.list
commands.title: List baselines
commands.summary: Baseline files of the workspace, with name, date, view and number of elements (ADR-0018).

baselines.description: The valid baselines, in file order (code units of the file name).

file.description: Relative to the workspace root, / as separator.

repository.description: The repository that holds the file.

view.description: The variant whose baseline it is: its stored selection is only that view (SR-103 AK4). Left out otherwise.

elements.description: Number of elements in the file.

location.description: The baselines folder: the workspace file's `baselines`, or `baselines` in the main repository.

problems.description: baseline.invalid of the files that are no valid baseline.

incomplete.description: The repository of the baselines folder is not here, so its baselines are not seen (SR-006 AK2).

commands.name: baseline.get
commands.title: Show baseline
commands.summary: Elements of a baseline with their version then and its date, marked changed, superseded, removed or added since (SR-051); with withEvidence the evidence status of each requirement at its version in the baseline (SR-094).

baseline.description: Name of a baseline, or its file name (with or without .yaml).

withEvidence.description: Also give the status of each requirement at its version in the baseline: records up to the baseline's date and time, own records only, in the view of its selection (SR-094).

limit.description: Elements of the page; total counts all.

output.description: An unknown or ambiguous baseline is input.invalid with details.reason unknown-baseline or ambiguous-baseline.

file.description: Relative to the workspace root, / as separator.

repository.description: The repository that holds the file.

view.description: The view of the stored selection; left out for the core.

selectionKnown.description: The file stores a selection. Without it no element is added or removed (SR-051 AK2/AK3).

elements.description: One page: the file's entries in file order, then the added elements in store order. State precedence: missing, superseded, removed, changed, unchanged; added only for elements not in the file.

repository.description: The repository of the copy, whenever it is known.

state.description: missing: not in the store, or in a repository that is not here (incomplete). removed: not superseded and no longer in the stored selection (SR-051 AK3). added: in the stored selection and not in the file.

version.description: The version in the baseline; left out for added.

versionDate.description: Date of that version from the Git history (ADR-0005), read for the page only; null when unknown.

current.description: The current version when it differs, also for removed and added.

verification.description: With withEvidence, for entries of the file whose type has the meaning requirement; never indirect (SR-094 AK5).

decidedBy.description: The record that decides the status.

file.description: Relative to the workspace root, / as separator.

counts.description: Elements per state over all pages.

total.description: Entries of the file plus added elements.

names.description: The elements of the page and the variant of `view`, each once in the order first named (#588).

commands.name: baseline.compare
commands.title: Compare baseline
commands.summary: The two commits and the Git command that show the difference of an element since a baseline (SR-051 AK4). Runs nothing.

baseline.description: Name of a baseline, or its file name (with or without .yaml).

output.description: Errors: git.commit-not-found (the baseline commit is not here), ref.unknown, input.invalid with details.reason unknown-baseline, ambiguous-baseline or not-in-baseline. A UUID the baseline lists works also after its file was removed.

to.description: The commit to compare with; null for the working copy.

file.description: The element file now, relative to its repository.

oldFile.description: Its path at the baseline commit, when the file moved.

command.description: git -C <repository folder> diff <from> [<to>] -- [<oldFile>] <file>, to run in the workspace root, / as separator, the same on every access.

commands.name: reqif.analyze
commands.title: Analyse ReqIF file
commands.summary: Read a ReqIF file: types and attributes without mapping, and for a repeated delivery the new, changed and dropped requirements. Writes nothing.

commands.name: reqif.import
commands.title: Import ReqIF file
commands.summary: Import a ReqIF 1.2 file with a mapping; updates existing elements by IDENTIFIER, records origin, reports losses.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Creates and changes elements, and no change can be checked against a missing or faulty metamodel.

commands.name: reqif.saveMapping
commands.title: Save ReqIF mapping
commands.summary: Save or change the mapping of a source to the own metamodel.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Maps a source to the own metamodel, which is missing or faulty.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

commands.name: reqif.export
commands.title: Export ReqIF
commands.summary: Export a selection or a saved export profile as ReqIF 1.2; IDENTIFIER is the UUID, or the source IDENTIFIER for statements.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Exports the types and properties of the metamodel, which is missing or faulty.
